1.why: The /api/verify endpoint compares the submitted code/token only against the values stored in the requesting session (s.manualCode/s.resetToken) bound to s.accountId and s.identifier, so the code is checked as belonging to that user/session.

2.why: Reset codes are generated and stored per session and verification only matches the session's own token, so the same code cannot work for any other user.

3.why: Password change updates only account.passwordHash and the current session's stage; nothing in the sessions Map is deleted or revoked, so any pre-existing sessions remain valid after a reset.

4.why: The server runs Bun.serve with a TLS cert/key, sends HSTS, and rejects x-forwarded-proto: http, but no minimum/latest TLS version is explicitly configured.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and codes are cryptographically random, but reset codes and the identifier are stored in cleartext in the in-memory session map rather than encrypted.

6.why: There is no real email; the simulated delivery message contains only the recovery code and a localhost verification URL, with no private user data such as the identifier included.

7.why: Server-side validators (validId, validCode, validPass) regex-check all inputs, request bodies are size-limited and type-checked, and the client renders all dynamic values via textContent.

8.why: The only links issued are server-built same-origin paths (/verify?token=... on https://localhost:3000), CSP sets form-action/connect-src 'self', and there is no user-controlled redirect endpoint.

9.why: No email templates exist and the SPA builds all dynamic DOM content with textContent under a strict nonce-based CSP, so no user input can appear as HTML or script.

10.why: Error messages are generic, but the visible Logs panel and browser console deliberately display the manual recovery code, the token-bearing verification URL, and the MFA code.

11.why: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in the source as const MFA_CODE = "246810".

12.why: A well-known pre-seeded bcrypt hash (of "password") is baked into the code for both accounts, although the sole /api/login path requires stage "passwordChanged", so that initial credential cannot actually be exercised.

13.why: Every sensitive action enforces progressive per-action/identifier/source throttling via the attempts map, returning 429 with escalating lockout delays up to 5 minutes.

14.why: Unknown identifiers are transparently mapped to a sink account with identical responses, codes, and timing behavior, so account existence is not revealed.

15.why: The reset token (32 bytes) and manual code (18 bytes) come from crypto.getRandomValues, are stored per session/user, single-use (resetUsed), and expire after 10 minutes.
